outcome: As of 13 October 2026 I found no source that settles the general question (smooth solutions of the 3D Vlasov–Maxwell system for data of arbitrary size, global in time); since 26 January 2024 the events are restricted results (a radiative variant, a half-space construction, a symmetry-restricted large-data result accepted at Annals of Mathematics, a small-data journal publication, a local-in-time journal publication) plus AI-linked work on steady states and on a namesake Maxwell conjecture, none of which is this problem.
problem_asks: The statement is 'Regularity of solutions of Vlasov–Maxwell equations', and read from the statement alone it asks the following. (1) Which objects: solutions of the Vlasov–Maxwell system, a transport equation for a particle distribution function coupled to Maxwell's equations for the self-generated electromagnetic field. The statement does not say which variant (classical or relativistic, with or without radiation reaction), which spatial dimension, or which class of initial data (smooth, small, large, compactly supported, symmetric). (2) Which property: regularity, i.e. whether solutions stay smooth or classical rather than developing singularities. (3) Over which time: no time qualifier is given; the working reading taken here is for all time (global regularity), since local-in-time regularity is standard and would not by itself answer a question posed as open. (4) Over which data: all admissible initial data, with no size, smallness or symmetry restriction stated, so a result for a restricted data class answers a restricted version of the question. The reading I adopted for the summary is the one the literature uses for this open problem (3 space dimensions, smooth data of unrestricted size, global in time, relativistic or classical), and I flag below where the bullet's wording leaves that open.

events.what_happened: Glassey and Strauss, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 92 (1986) 59–90: a continuation criterion for the 3D relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. Classical (C¹) solutions do not develop singularities as long as the momentum support of the distribution stays bounded. I did not open the 1986 paper; the statement is taken from the abstract of Bouchut–Golse–Pallard (2003), which cites it.
events.delivers: Conditional global C¹ regularity for the 3D relativistic system, provided the momentum support stays bounded on bounded time intervals. This is a continuation criterion, not an unconditional global result.
events.remains: Whether the momentum support stays bounded for arbitrary smooth data, which is the open part of problem_asks in the 3D relativistic case; the classical system and general size of data are also untouched.

events.what_happened: The manuscript 'Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system' (the only manuscript in this family) claims global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions of the one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system in three space and three momentum dimensions, for every smooth admissible datum (Theorem 1.1, thm:global). A datum is a nonnegative smooth particle density f0 with compact support, and fields E0, B0 with all spatial derivatives bounded and finite energy, satisfying the two Gauss constraints (div E0 = rho of f0, div B0 = 0). Nonzero total charge is allowed. For each finite T the solution has f smooth on [0,T] x R^3 x R^3, E and B smooth on [0,T] x R^3, f with compact phase-space support on [0,T], and the constraints hold for all time. The proof has two parts. (i) A signed momentum-increment estimate along characteristics (Proposition 1.1, eq. bootstrap): |V_X(t2) - V_X(t1)| <= M P sqrt(t2 - t1) + A (t2 - t1) S(w), with S(w) = P^2 log(2+P)/w, proved by a bootstrap and continuity argument (setup.tex, direction.tex, selection.tex, closure.tex). Since the resulting lower bounds on the time needed to double the maximal momentum have a divergent sum, finite-time growth of momentum is excluded. (ii) A local-theory and bounded-momentum continuation statement (Proposition 1.2, continuation.tex). The manuscript obtains it from the Glassey–Strauss criterion as quoted by Luk and Strain, after a finite-horizon modification of the initial fields: the Coulomb field is kept and a vacuum Maxwell solution vanishing on the particle region is subtracted.
events.delivers: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness on each finite time interval for the relativistic one-species Vlasov–Maxwell system in three space dimensions, with no restriction on size, symmetry or total charge. The restrictions that come with it: (a) the initial particle density must be smooth and compactly supported, so noncompact particle data are not covered; (b) the fields must have all spatial derivatives bounded and finite energy (in L^2), so fields without finite energy are not covered; (c) uniqueness holds only in the class of classical solutions as the manuscript defines it (C^1 solutions with E, B continuous into L^2); (d) the bound on the momentum support is available on each finite interval only and may grow with that interval; (e) the equations are written in a normalization with the usual 4 pi absorbed into the fields and charge density. The manuscript says the result 'resolves the large-data global classical regularity problem for this model'. disputes.summary: Gemini's role in the VML equilibrium work is stated differently in two papers by the same author group. Ilin arXiv 2603.15929 says Gemini DeepThink 'generated the proof from a conjecture' and 'generated the initial natural-language proof of the theorem'. Ilin and Hu arXiv 2603.25832 says the proofs 'were obtained with the assistance of Gemini DeepThink'. Both concern steady states, not the VM regularity bullet.

Attribution of the AI-found counterexample in the Maxwell electrostatics paper. The paper says the idea was 'suggested by an LLM (OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol)'; press reports say GPT-5.6 Sol proposed the geometric idea and the three authors did the analysis; a co-author's post, reported by Habr and reposted by Greg Brockman, says the counterexample was found by AI and that mathematicians only communicated it. Only the paper is an authors' account; the others are press or social-media reports I did not open.

The Ilin VML project reports several figures: $200 total (abstract); $200 per month for the Claude Max plan (Section 3); about $6,300 API-equivalent with prompt caching and about $42,700 without (Sections 5, 8); $325 subscription in the ICML listing (search excerpt, not opened). The paper does not reconcile them in the parts I read.

Data class for the Glassey–Schaeffer 2D/2½D large-data result: Luk–Strain (arXiv 1406.0168 abstract) describe regular data with compact momentum support; a search excerpt of a 2½D abstract says global existence for smooth data of unrestricted size. Not resolved; the 2D/2½D result is not the 3D question in either case.

summary: I ran 38 web searches and opened 27 sources. The bullet names no dimension, variant, data class or time scope, so I read it as the standard open question: whether smooth solutions of the 3D Vlasov–Maxwell system with data of arbitrary size stay regular for all time. The 2004 Glassey lecture (abstract), Ben-Artzi–Pankavich–Zhang (2021, abstract) and Constantin–Grayer (June 2025 introduction, 'has been studied extensively, but remains unsolved') all describe this as open, and I found no 2026 source claiming a proof. Since 26 January 2024 the events are restricted: Constantin and Grayer prove unconditional large-data global regularity for a radiation-reaction variant (arXiv April 2025; Princeton portal lists CMP 407(7) art. 145, July 2026, Springer page not opened), which changes the equation and so is not the classical question; Jang and Kim (September 2025) construct global classical solutions in a half-space; Cheverry and Ibrahim (arXiv June 2023; journal online September 2024, vol. 41 2025) give only local-in-time theory; Bigorgne (arXiv August 2022; Analysis & PDE 2025) covers small data; and Wang's large-data cylindrical-symmetry result (arXiv March 2022, v2 July 2026) was accepted by Annals of Mathematics on 15 July 2026, which is a symmetry-restricted class. Pre-window results are all conditional, small-data, symmetric, near-neutral, lower-dimensional or local: Glassey–Strauss 1986 (momentum-support criterion), Glassey–Strauss 1987 (small data), Glassey–Schaeffer 1988 (3D nearly neutral charge), Glassey–Schaeffer 1997–98 (2D and 2½D), Luk–Strain 2014 and 2016 (continuation criteria), Sospedra-Alfonso and Illner 2012 (bounded density), Wang 2018 (small data, massive variant), Wang 2020 (spherical symmetry, arXiv comment 'not for publication'), Wei–Yang 2020 (large field, small density; CMP 2021). AI: no source I read credits an AI system with any part of the Vlasov–Maxwell regularity mathematics, and no AI-linked work on this bullet turned up. The AI-linked events I found are about other questions and are recorded as discounted: Ilin's Lean formalisation of the Vlasov–Maxwell–Landau equilibrium (March 2026), where Gemini DeepThink generated the proof, Claude Code wrote the Lean and Aristotle closed 111 lemmas; Ilin and Hu's neural particle paper (March 2026), whose equilibrium proofs were 'obtained with the assistance of Gemini DeepThink'; Miller's Lean formalisation of the nonlinear Vlasov equation (July 2026), with the AI system unnamed in the abstract; and Arathoon, Ball and Kvalheim's disproof of Maxwell's electrostatic conjecture (July 2026), where the authors say the idea was 'suggested by an LLM (OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol)'. Close calls: (i) the bullet's wording leaves dimension, variant and data size open, and if it were read as 'some regularity of some solution' the local and weak-solution results would count, and a result of the 1986–2003 criteria type would be a candidate; (ii) the 2D/2½D data class is described differently by two sources; (iii) Gemini's role in the VML papers is worded differently in each; (iv) the Ilin project's cost figures vary. I checked the Springer and DOI pages for the 2026 Constantin–Grayer paper and the 2021 Wei–Yang paper, and both redirected to a login page, so their journal status rests on the Princeton portal and citing references. I also noticed, in an AI search, a September 2026 OpenAI claim about the forced 3D Navier–Stokes equations; it does not concern this problem, and I did not open it.
competing_reading: A reader who takes the bullet as 'regularity of solutions' in any sense would count the 1986–2003 conditional criteria, the 1988 near-neutral result, the 2012 bounded-density criterion, the 2014–2016 continuation criteria, Cheverry–Ibrahim's local theory and the in-window Annals/CMP items as progress, and the answer would be 'partly settled for restricted classes' rather than 'open'. A reader who takes the bullet as the 3D large-data classical question counts only restricted results and calls it open. A reader who takes the 2D/2½D results as the target would find it resolved before the window. The AI question has a similar split: a reader who counts formalisation or assistance as load-bearing would count the Ilin and Ilin–Hu items, but they concern steady states, not this bullet.
what_would_settle_it: The wording of the Wikipedia bullet's linked article and its edit history, to fix the intended variant and dimension; the Springer records for CMP 407 art. 145 (Constantin–Grayer) and CMP 383 (Wei–Yang) to confirm journal status; the Annals volume for Wang's cylindrical paper and whether Part II exists; an arXiv listing search in math.AP for 2026 Vlasov–Maxwell papers with the date filter, which my web search could not do; and the full texts of the restricted results to confirm their hypotheses. For the AI question, the authors' own account of any 2026 classical or relativistic large-data claim.

event.what_happened: The manuscript 'Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system' (the only manuscript in this family) claims global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions of the one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system in three space and three momentum dimensions, for every smooth admissible datum (Theorem 1.1, thm:global). A datum is a nonnegative smooth particle density f0 with compact support, and fields E0, B0 with all spatial derivatives bounded and finite energy, satisfying the two Gauss constraints (div E0 = rho of f0, div B0 = 0). Nonzero total charge is allowed. For each finite T the solution has f smooth on [0,T] x R^3 x R^3, E and B smooth on [0,T] x R^3, f with compact phase-space support on [0,T], and the constraints hold for all time. The proof has two parts. (i) A signed momentum-increment estimate along characteristics (Proposition 1.1, eq. bootstrap): |V_X(t2) - V_X(t1)| <= M P sqrt(t2 - t1) + A (t2 - t1) S(w), with S(w) = P^2 log(2+P)/w, proved by a bootstrap and continuity argument (setup.tex, direction.tex, selection.tex, closure.tex). Since the resulting lower bounds on the time needed to double the maximal momentum have a divergent sum, finite-time growth of momentum is excluded. (ii) A local-theory and bounded-momentum continuation statement (Proposition 1.2, continuation.tex). The manuscript obtains it from the Glassey–Strauss criterion as quoted by Luk and Strain, after a finite-horizon modification of the initial fields: the Coulomb field is kept and a vacuum Maxwell solution vanishing on the particle region is subtracted.

judgement.why: The statement names no variant, dimension or data class, so it is read broadly: regularity of Vlasov–Maxwell solutions in general. Small-data, symmetric, near-neutral, low-dimensional and large-field/small-density results are cases; continuation criteria and local theory are reductions or standard theory (none); radiative, half-space, toy-model, VML-equilibrium, mean-field Vlasov and the electrostatic Maxwell namesake are variants or different problems. The close call is openai-math-362: it claims the canonical Glassey–Strauss problem (3D relativistic, compactly supported smooth data, finite-energy fields, no size restriction), which many would treat as the whole question; I scored it case because the statement's wording does not restrict to the relativistic system or to compactly supported data, and the manuscript itself excludes noncompact particle data and other variants. It is unreviewed (Lean build is not digestion) and doubtful given the omitted steps, and its role is generated per the README. Wang's cylindrical result is pre-snapshot (arXiv March 2022; Annals acceptance is not new mathematics). Ilin's Gemini generation and the GPT-5.6 Sol idea are credited on their own events but those events are variants.
judgement.doubts: If the statement is read as the canonical 3D relativistic compact-support problem, openai-math-362 would be whole (claimed) rather than case; the record cannot fix the intended reading. The Lean formalisation of openai-math-362 was not checked for sorry-freeness or statement alignment. Claude Code in the Ilin event only formalised and is not credited.
